newsitem.title: USA: AMR to accept arbitration with pilots.
newsitem.headline: AMR to accept arbitration with pilots.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines said on Friday that it will accept the proffer of binding arbitration issued by the National Mediation Board, regarding its talks with the Allied Pilots Association.
The airline said acceptance of arbitration is subject to the pilot's union joining the airline to accept the board's offer.
If either party rejects the board's proffer of binding arbitration, a 30-day "cooling-off" period commences, American Airlines said.
American Airlines said the union would be free to strike and the airline would be free to implement new pay and work rules, if an agreement is not reached during the cooling off period.

The Allied Pilots Association rejected a proposed four-year contract from the airline on January 8, 1997, when 5,046 members of the union voted against ratifying the contract and only 3,197 voted in favor of it.
American Airlines said it planned to buy 103 jets from Boeing Co and take out options to buy 527 more if the pilots approved the contract.
Representatives for the Allied Pilots Association could not immediately be reached.
